newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Boeing challenge could spark new EU-U.S. row.
newsitem.headline: Boeing challenge could spark new EU-U.S. row.

text.p: The European Commission's challenge to the merger between U.S. aircraft makers Boeing and McDonnell Douglas Corp could spark off yet another row between the European Union and its major trading partner.
"Were the Commission to seek remedies, it would risk producing tensions between the two sides," a senior Commission official said on Wednesday.

European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert unexpectedly attacked the $13.3 billion, stock-for-stock merger, saying that at first sight it could strengthen Boeing's already dominant position in Europe.

The reaction, only two days after the deal was announced, was viewed by some Commission officials and antitrust lawyers as reflecting a political desire to protect the European consortium Airbus as much as fair competition.
"I find it hard to believe that the EU is a neutral party. It has an interest in promoting the European industry, in promoting Airbus," one Brussels-based lawyer said.

Van Miert's comments come amid increasing criticism in Europe about huge subsidies being paid to the defence aviation industry in the U.S. which are seen as spilling over to the civil aviation sector.
"The Americans support their industry by passing huge military orders whose prices are generously calculated," the Commission official said.
"Competition is bloody in the sector," he added, noting that it was often difficult to make a clear distinction between the military and the civil aviation businesses of an aircraft maker.
The merger of the two U.S. aerospace companies would create the world's leading aerospace and defence company.

Europe's civil aviation Airbus Industrie consortium and U.S. defence aircraft maker Lockheed Martin are its closest competitors in an industry where consolidation appears inevitable. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
